false_success_traps: A page that asks you to log in or sign up as a member is not a listing and not a confirmation.
Reading the privacy page is not a request. On 2026-11-16 the page pointed to third-party sites and showed no form of its own.
State subdomains are public-record explainer and index pages. They are not proof that a person listing exists.
This project's automation never reports a ThePublicIndex request as sent. It always hands the work to a person.
name: ThePublicIndex

opt_out_routes.note: Use the privacy address for covered-person requests. Also use it when the removal form is blocked or incomplete.

opt_out_url_check.note: The page loaded as "Your Privacy Choices". Its text now says privacy requests are handled by the third-party site a search was sent to. No removal form was seen in the page as fetched. Project notes from 2026-07-09 describe a removal form here, so the page may have changed.

quirks: A sent form is not a removal claim. Wait until a check confirms the listing is gone.
State subdomains are public-record explainer and index pages. They are not proof that a person listing exists.
The form posts to members.thepublicindex.org/removeMyData/. It asks for first name, last name, and state. City is optional.
steps: Open the ThePublicIndex "Your Privacy Choices" page.
Read what the page asks for today. On 2026-11-16 it said requests are handled by the third-party site that a search was sent to.
If that applies to you, make the request on that third-party site's own privacy page.
If the page shows a removal form instead, only send it when the record shown is clearly yours.
Covered-person requests can go by email to privacy@thepublicindex.org.
Do not count the request as done until a later check shows the listing is gone.
playbook.suppression_lane: Use the ThePublicIndex privacy choices form at /optout. Treat as assisted until a later recheck verifies the listing is gone.
